datasets.description: Ultra-wide 40mm f/2.8, unobstructed, IMX571 bin1 -- severely oversampled control for the R2 pixelization floor (native HFR_min well under the 0.70px floor). Cygnus, rich wide field, capped at mag<=10.5 so the ~39deg diagonal FOV catalog query (design risk R5) stays tractable.
135mm f/2.0, unobstructed, IMX571 bin1 -- another severely-oversampled R2 point at a different focal length. Heart/Soul Nebula region (Cassiopeia), rich field.
250mm f/4.9 RedCat-class refractor, unobstructed, IMX533 bin1 -- the third and last R2 (pixelization floor) point. Orion's Belt, mid-density field.
550mm f/5.5 apo, unobstructed, IMX571 bin1. M24 (Sagittarius Star Cloud) -- one of the densest star fields on the sky; exercises the crowded-field merge/blend golden-policy paths.
1000mm f/7.1 apo, unobstructed, IMX455 bin1. Auriga, mid-density field -- the L-class (mid focal length, well-sampled) recall/precision anchor's rich sibling.

Same optics as D05 (1000mm f/7.1, unobstructed, IMX533 bin1) but pointed at the North Galactic Pole -- an intrinsically star-poor field (~tens of stars), exercising StarFieldIsExhausted and the star-count probe.
RC10-class, 2000mm f/8, 0.47 obstruction, IMX533 bin1. Double Cluster (Perseus), rich field, heavily undersampled donuts -- the first donut* = true dataset.
C11-class SCT, 2800mm f/10, 0.34 obstruction, IMX571 bin1. General Hercules field, mid density -- the first detectionBinning=2 dataset (in-focus HFR crosses the DetectionBinningResolver threshold).
C14-class SCT, 3800mm f/10.7, 0.34 obstruction, IMX294 bin1. Cepheus, rich field near the extreme long-focal-length end of the matrix.

RC16-class, 3250mm f/8, 0.47 obstruction, IMX533 bin1. Virgo, sparse field (~tens of stars) at long focal length -- the donut-aware sibling of D06's star-count-probe stress test. Limiting magnitude 18.0 puts the 20th-brightest star near the faint end, which is what makes this dataset's expected exposure ~17s with the band top clamping at the recommender's 30s ceiling -- D10, not D16, is the dataset scenario S3 uses to exercise ExposureRecommender.CappedByAbsoluteLimit.

RC10-class, 2000mm f/8, 0.47 obstruction, IMX585 captured at AF-bin 2 (detection binning stays 1) -- separates AF/capture binning from detection binning. Cygnus, rich field. Seeing set to 3.0" (top of the allowed 2.5-3.0" range): at 2.5" the extreme-frame captured HFR falls just under DonutHeuristic.HeavyDefocusHFR (9px), which would derive donut*=false; at 3.0" it clears with margin, matching this row's intended donut*=true.
C14-class SCT, 3800mm f/10.7, 0.34 obstruction, IMX585 captured at AF-bin 2 -- D11's counterpart where BOTH AF-bin and detection binning land at 2. Cassiopeia, rich field.

200mm apo, 1800mm f/9, UNOBSTRUCTED (the donut control), IMX571 bin1. Lyra, mid-density field. A 1800mm unobstructed refractor makes filled discs at extreme defocus, not donuts -- if any product signal recommends donut detection here, that is a defect, not a preference.
CDK14-class, 2563mm f/7.2, 0.47 obstruction, IMX455 bin1. Perseus (Alpha Persei cluster region), rich field.
CDK20-class, 3454mm f/6.8, 0.47 obstruction, IMX571 bin1. Cepheus flare (Iris Nebula / dark-cloud complex region), mid-density field near the matrix's longest well-obstructed focal length.

Same optics as D04 (550mm f/5.5, unobstructed, IMX571 bin1) but through a 3nm Hα narrowband filter. Heart Nebula (Cassiopeia), rich Hα field. Hα passes ~64-107x less flux than L, so the derived exposure is expected to sit near ExposureRecommender's 30s absolute ceiling (CappedByAbsoluteLimit). NOTE: the derived exposure lands at the 0.5s floor despite the 3nm filter, because ExposureRecommender's sensitivity metric is the NTarget=20th-brightest star's SNR and a 2.9deg field always contains 20 bright stars. D16 is therefore the narrowband-realism dataset, not the 30s-cap dataset (that role moved to D10).

Same optics as D14 (CDK14-class, 2563mm f/7.2, 0.47 obstruction, IMX533 bin1) but through a 5nm OIII narrowband filter. Cygnus X star-forming complex, rich field. Narrowband datasets inherit their optical class's expected precision/recall bands (L47 here).

550mm f/5.5 apo, unobstructed, IMX571 bin1. M24 at limiting magnitude 15.5 -- D04's field pushed 1.5 mag deeper. F33's SHEDDING class: a dense field carries enough stars that the optimizer can raise the acceptance gate and still clear the NHard=3 floor, which is the headroom the rest of the synthetic bank lacks (median min-frame detections 7, vs 37 on the real bank). The deep limiting magnitude supplies the faint near-threshold tail whose MEMBERSHIP changes with focus position -- detected near focus where flux is concentrated, lost at the wings -- which is the mechanism that makes shedding buy a tighter sigma_focus on real rigs.

1000mm f/7.1 apo, unobstructed, IMX455 bin1. Cygnus star cloud at limiting magnitude 16.0 -- the SECOND shedder, on a different optic and a different field, so a finding about the shedding regime cannot rest on one rig's geometry or one pointing's crowding.

550mm f/5.5 apo, unobstructed, IMX571 bin1. D18's rig and field at limiting magnitude 12.0 -- THE CONTROL, designed before the experiment (wave 3's D05 lesson: only the row whose job is not to move exposed the seed leak). Dense enough to clear the hard floor, but bright-dominated: with no faint near-threshold tail, every star is detected at every focus position, so the sampled population does not change with defocus and shedding buys no sigma_focus. It isolates the FAINT TAIL from mere density -- if D20 sheds too, density alone explains the regime and the faint-tail mechanism is refuted.
